claims.head: The Avalanche should tilt the ice
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Avalanche have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Maple Leafs one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Avalanche’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

notes.text: Zachary L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.
Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 59% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 45:15 together, up from 48% with Blankenburg.
Max Domi is on long-term injured reserve and has not played this season.
Jack Roslovic is day to day (lower-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 19 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Avalanche go in tied for second in the Central with 22 points, the Maple Leafs seventh in the Atlantic with 18 points.

TOR.head: Not an easy night for the Maple Leafs
TOR.body: Even though Toronto gets Tanev back and has home-ice advantage, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs’ best way through is keeping dangerous shots away.

COL.head: Advantage, the Avalanche

story.head: MacKinnon’s favorite opponent
paras: The Maple Leafs won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-3 in Colorado on Oct 10. The Maple Leafs are on a three-game losing streak, while the Avalanche (10-6-2) beat Detroit 4-0 on Saturday. Going in, the Avalanche are third in the Central (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Leafs seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 19th).

The Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest) and get their defensemen shooting (2nd). Colorado has scored 4.00 goals a game, the third most in the league. As for the Maple Leafs, they get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd) and take a lot of low-quality shots (31st). The Avalanche are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, especially the Avalanche (1st), so expect an open game.

Nathan MacKinnon (10 G / 20 A / 30 P in 18 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is fifth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and a point in seven straight games against Toronto. Artturi Lehkonen (12 G / 5 A / 17 P in 18 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, fifth in the NHL. Auston Matthews (11 G / 16 A / 27 P in 19 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is sixth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. William Nylander (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind.
Mackenzie Blackwood (9-3-1 / .901 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Colorado, and Sergei Bobrovsky (3-7-2 / .886 SV% in 12 GS) for Toronto.
The Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Maple Leafs do.

items.text: The Maple Leafs are newly without Jack Roslovic, have been without Kirill Marchenko and Nick Blankenburg for several games, and have had to make do without Max Domi all season.
Artturi Lehkonen has twelve goals on chances worth about 6.5 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
William Nylander is one point from passing George Armstrong for seventh on the Maple Leafs’ all-time scoring list.
Nick Paul has one goal on chances worth about 3.5 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
